title: Percent change and CAGR
explanation: **Welcome to Level 10: finance!** A streaming startup is pitching investors, and its subscriber numbers need the two growth measures every finance interview asks about: **percent change** year over year, and **CAGR**, the steady yearly growth rate that would get you from start to finish.

tasks.prompt: In C3, work out 2022's growth: (new − old) ÷ old: =(B3-B2)/B2.
tasks.teach: **Percent change = (new − old) ÷ old.** The brackets matter: without them Excel would divide first. The cell is already formatted as a percent, so 0.3 shows as 30.0%.
hints: New is B3, old is B2.
Copy C3, then paste into C4:C6.

tasks.prompt: In E2, work out the total growth from 2021 to 2025: =B6/B2-1.
tasks.teach: **new ÷ old − 1** is the same as (new − old) ÷ old, just shorter. Subscribers more than doubled, so it's over 100%.

tasks.prompt: Last one: in F2, work out the CAGR over the 4 years: =(B6/B2)^(1/4)-1.
tasks.teach: **CAGR (compound annual growth rate) = (end ÷ start)^(1 ÷ years) − 1.** The **^** sign means "to the power of". From 2021 to 2025 is **4** years of growth, not 5: count the gaps, not the years. CAGR smooths out the bumpy year-by-year growth into one steady rate.
hints: 4 years of growth, so the power is 1/4.

recap: Percent change is (new − old) ÷ old. CAGR is (end ÷ start)^(1 ÷ years) − 1, counting the gaps between years. ^ means "to the power of".
